sections.h2: Why does Nassau County's growth matter for a home sale?
sections.html:
QuickFacts reports 106,879 residents in 2025 against 90,352 counted in the 2020 census, a rise of 18.3 percent on the revised base, inside 648.68 square miles of land.

Survey data puts the typical owned home at $382,800, with 82.7 percent of homes owner-occupied and carrying costs of $1,849 a month for those with a mortgage. The county counted 49,001 housing units in 2025 and 1,060 building permits that year.

  • Households: 39,307, averaging 2.47 people.
  • Residents 65 and older: 26.7 percent.
  • Mean commute: 30.1 minutes.

Ask the property appraiser how your parcel's assessed value compares with its just value, since that gap is what a sale erases.

sections.h2: What does the Nassau County Tax Collector say about estimating a tax bill?
sections.html:
The tax collector tells buyers never to treat a seller's past or current tax amount as a forecast. A new owner does not inherit the prior owner's assessed value, Save Our Homes cap or exemptions.

The same page explains that the property appraiser can help estimate upcoming taxes, but that office does not see non-ad valorem assessments such as community development district fees. Those fees are added to the bill separately, and the estimate must come from the district itself. If your Nassau neighborhood sits inside a district, tell your buyer so that the closing numbers include it.

Sellers can use this to set expectations early. A buyer reading your old bill may expect a lower figure than reality, and a clear note about reassessment avoids a surprise at the table.

sections.h2: Who lives in Nassau County, and where do they work?
sections.html:
Nassau County skews toward families who own their homes and commute. QuickFacts lists median household income of $89,804 for 2020 to 2024 and per capita income of $47,685, with 8.7 percent of residents below the poverty line. Broadband subscriptions reach 94.6 percent of households, and 87.4 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

Employer establishments numbered 2,261 in 2023, with total employment of 21,651. Accommodation and food services brought in $613,642 thousand in 2022, and retail sales were $1,305,109 thousand, or $13,341 per resident.

  • Residents under 18: 18.8 percent.
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or higher: 35.6 percent.
  • Foreign-born share: 3.9 percent.

Long commutes and fast growth mean that buyers often arrive from other parts of Florida or other states, so expect questions about new construction, district fees and taxes.

sections.h2: What is the Nassau County bill-and-discount schedule?
sections.html:
Payment runs on a sliding monthly discount that ends March 31. Anything left unpaid becomes delinquent April 1.

  • November payment: 4 percent off.
  • December: 3 percent.
  • January: 2 percent.
  • February: 1 percent.

Florida's revenue department places the property appraiser's notice of proposed taxes in August, public budget hearings in September and October, and tax bills in November. A value challenge goes to the clerk's value adjustment board petition process within 25 days of the notice of proposed property taxes.

For questions about a bill, call the tax collector's tax department at 904-491-7420, the number printed on its partial payment page.

sections.h2: What should a Nassau County seller tell a buyer about the tax bill?
sections.html:
Give the buyer the parcel's real situation, not a rule of thumb. The tax collector's own advice is that a buyer should never rely on a seller's current or past tax amount, and a clear explanation protects both sides before a contract is signed.

  • Say whether a homestead exemption and a capped value are on the roll today, and that neither carries over.
  • Name any community development district or other non-ad valorem assessment, and give the buyer the district's contact so the buyer can ask for the amount.
  • Explain whether taxes are escrowed. If a lender pays, partial payments are discouraged and the lender sets the timing.
  • Mention any unpaid prior year, since the lien follows the land.

A buyer who learns these things at the start is less likely to ask for a credit late in the deal. Sellers who offer a plain written summary, along with a printout from the property appraiser's estimate tool, make closing day smoother. A tax bill estimate from the appraiser will leave out district fees, so ask the title company to add them.

sections.h2: How do exemptions and capped values work for Nassau owners?
sections.html:
Exemptions come from the property appraiser, who takes applications each year. With 26.7 percent of residents age 65 or older and 8,635 veterans, the senior and military programs see steady use in Nassau.

A county or city may adopt an extra senior exemption within an income limit, and another ordinance may help long-term residents with lower-value homes. Ask the property appraiser which of these apply in Nassau County or its towns.

  • A $5,000 reduction in assessed value for a disabled ex-servicemember.
  • A homestead discount for veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.
  • A possible full homestead exemption for total and permanent disability.

A rented unit cannot keep homestead, so a landlord selling a former residence should confirm what is on the roll.

sections.h2: Is a partial payment allowed in Nassau County?
sections.html:
It is allowed, with costs spelled out by the collector. Section 197.374 allows partial payment on a current-year bill, and the office accepts them from November 1 through March 31 with the postmark counting.

  • The account loses the early-payment discount, even if the balance is later cleared in a discount month.
  • Escrowed accounts paid by a lender should not make partial payments.
  • Accounts on an installment plan should skip partial payments.
  • Whatever is unpaid on April 1 enters the delinquent process of advertising and a certificate sale.

To set one up, contact the tax department at 904-491-7420 or taxes@nassautaxes.com. Payments can be made in person, by mail or online once the account is set up.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Nassau County taxes?
sections.html:
The tax collector must hold a tax certificate sale on or before June 1, and it is conducted online on the LienHub platform. The table lays out the terms as the office prints them.

Nassau tax certificate terms (source: nassautaxes.com delinquent real estate taxes page)
ItemAs printed
Sale deadlineOn or before June 1 each year
BiddingDownward on interest, starting at 18 percent; lowest bidder wins
Minimum earned5 percent until accrued interest exceeds it; zero-interest bids earn zero
Lien statusEnforceable first lien on the real estate
ValiditySeven years from issuance
Tax deed applicationWhen two or more years have passed since delinquency

To remove the lien, the owner pays the collector all delinquent tax plus interest, costs and other charges. State law also bars a certificate holder from demanding payment from the owner for two years after April 1 of the issuance year, and a deed application carries a $75 fee. Homestead land with a small delinquency goes to the county rather than to a bidder.

sections.h2: How do homestead rules and deed taxes affect a Nassau County sale?
sections.html:
The standard exemption takes up to $50,000 off taxable value, filed by March 1, and the capped assessment growth was 2.7 percent for 2026 per the state chart. A buyer's value starts over after a sale.

Deed stamps in Nassau follow section 201.02 at 70 cents on every $100 of price. Liability sits with all parties to the deed, and payment goes to the clerk at recording.

faqs.q: Does a new Nassau County owner get the seller's tax amount?
faqs.a: No. The tax collector says the buyer does not benefit from the prior owner's assessed value, Save Our Homes cap or exemptions, so past bills are not a safe estimate.

faqs.q: Do community development district fees show on the appraiser's estimate?
faqs.a: No. The appraiser has no access to non-ad valorem assessments, so ask the district for its amount, which is then added to the tax bill.

faqs.q: Do I lose the discount if I make a partial payment in Nassau County?
faqs.a: Yes. Per the tax collector, the account is no longer eligible for discount even if the rest is paid during a discount month. Partial payments run November 1 through March 31.

faqs.q: When does Nassau County sell tax certificates?
faqs.a: The sale is held by June 1 each year on the LienHub site. Bids start at 18 percent and fall, and the lowest rate takes the certificate.

faqs.q: How long before a tax deed can be sought on a Nassau County parcel?
faqs.a: The certificate holder may apply when two or more years have passed since delinquency. Until then, the owner can redeem by paying taxes, interest, costs and charges.
